habitat: Pairs in coastal bush and dune forest, especially dense thickets with creepers. It is not secretive.
summary: A locally common, near-endemic resident. Dark eye, yellow-green upperparts, a buff wash on the underparts especially the throat, and a yellow-and-green undertail rather than a white one. The pair calls together, one a fast tritritritrit and the other punk-punk-punk. No openly licensed Kruger photograph was found.

similar.note: Bar-throated Apalis has a pale yellow eye, white outer tail feathers and darker upperparts. Rudd’s Apalis has a dark eye and a yellow-green undertail.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^12=4096 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 2048–8192.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: More yellow-green above than Bar-throated Apalis.

underparts.pattern: Buff wash, especially on the throat.

tail.shape: undertail yellow and green, not white

viewNotes.note: Yellow-green apalis with a dark eye in dense thicket.
Dark eye. The throat has a buff wash.
Buff-washed underparts and a yellow-green undertail.

calls.description: One bird gives a fast, loud tritritritritritritrit while the other calls punk-punk-punk at the same time. Grade A from near St Lucia, KwaZulu-Natal.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed from Newman’s resident wording. Population figures were left unchanged.
